title.en: Volume 43 Biographies 24: Jiang Xiao, He Changyu, Xie Yao, Wang Siyuan
title.raw: 卷四十三 列傳第二十四 江斆 何昌㝢 謝𤅢 王思遠 Volume 43 Biographies 24: Jiang Xiao, He Changyu, Xie Yao, Wang Siyuan

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷四十三‧列傳第二十四

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 43, Biographies 24
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 43, Biographies 24

sentences.zh: 江斆 何昌㝢 謝𤅢 王思遠

translations.literal: Jiang Xiao, He Changyu, Xie Yao, Wang Siyuan
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xiao, He Changyu, Xie Yao, and Wang Siyuan

sentences.zh: 江斆字叔文，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Xiao, courtesy name Shuwen, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xiao, whose courtesy name was Shuwen, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖湛，宋左光祿大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhan was Left Director of the Bureau of Honors and Three Ministers of Equal Court Rank in Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jiang Zhan served in the Song as Left Director of the Bureau of Honors and as a Three Ministers of Equal Court Rank.

sentences.zh: 父恁，著作郎，爲太初所殺。

translations.literal: His father Nian was a Composition Official and was killed by Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiang Nian was a Composition Official and was killed by Liu Ziye (Emperor Taichu).

sentences.zh: 斆母文帝女淮陽公主。

translations.literal: Xiao's mother was the Princess of Huaiyang, a daughter of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao's mother was the Princess of Huaiyang, a daughter of Emperor Wen of Song.

sentences.zh: 幼以戚屬召見，孝武謂謝莊曰：「此小兒方當爲名器。」

translations.literal: In childhood he was summoned for audience as a kinsman of the imperial house; Emperor Xiaowu said to Xie Zhuang: "This boy will surely become a vessel of renown."
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was brought to court because of his imperial kinship, and Emperor Xiaowu told Xie Zhuang, "This boy is destined to become a man of great standing."

sentences.zh: 少有美譽。

translations.literal: In youth he enjoyed a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Even in his youth he enjoyed an excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休範臨州，辟迎主簿，不就。

translations.literal: When Prince Guiyang Xiufan took charge of the province, he invited Xiao as Master of Reception, but Xiao did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guiyang of Xiufan assumed his provincial post, he invited Xiao to serve as Master of Reception, but Xiao declined.

sentences.zh: 尚孝武女臨汝公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Linru, daughter of Emperor Xiaowu, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Linru, a daughter of Emperor Xiaowu, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Imperial Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 除著作郎，太子舍人，丹陽丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Composition Official, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Assistant Magistrate of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Composition Official, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Assistant Magistrate of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 時袁粲爲尹，見斆歎曰：「風流不墜，政在江郎。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Can was chief magistrate of the capital; seeing Xiao he sighed and said: "The elegant tradition has not fallen—it rests with Master Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Can was serving as metropolitan magistrate; when he met Xiao he exclaimed, "The refined tradition has not died out—it lives on in Master Jiang.

sentences.zh: 」數與晏賞，留連日夜。

translations.literal: " He often feasted and enjoyed pleasures with him, lingering day and night.
translations.idiomatic: " He often shared wine and conversation with him, keeping company late into the night for days on end.

sentences.zh: 遷安成王撫軍記室，祕書丞，中書郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Recorder of the Pacification Army staff of Prince Ancheng, Secretary Director, and Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Recorder on the Pacification Army staff of Prince Ancheng, then Secretary Director, and finally Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 斆庶祖母王氏老疾，斆視膳嘗藥，七十餘日不解衣。

translations.literal: Xiao's secondary grandmother, the Lady Wang, was aged and ill; Xiao supervised her meals and tasted her medicine, and for more than seventy days did not remove his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: When his father's concubine-mother, Lady Wang, grew old and fell ill, Xiao personally attended her meals and tasted her medicine, going more than seventy days without undressing.

sentences.zh: 及累居內官，每以侍養陳請，朝廷優其朝直。

translations.literal: When he successively held inner-court offices, he each time submitted a request to attend and nurse her, and the court granted him leniency in court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: After he rose through a series of inner-court posts, he repeatedly petitioned to be allowed to nurse her at home, and the court relaxed his requirements for attending morning audience.

sentences.zh: 尋轉安成王驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the Rapid Cavalry staff of Prince Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Attendant of the Masters of Writing on Prince Ancheng's Rapid Cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 初，湛娶褚秀之女，被遣，褚淵爲衞軍，重斆爲人，先通音意，引爲長史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhan had married the daughter of Chu Xiu and was dismissed; Chu Yuan was General of the Guard, valued Xiao's character, communicated with him beforehand, and appointed him Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jiang Zhan had married a daughter of Chu Xiu and was later dismissed; when Chu Yuan became General of the Guard, he admired Xiao's character, opened relations with him in advance, and appointed him Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: He was additionally made General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given the rank of General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 從帝立，隨府轉司空長史，領臨淮太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When the deposed emperor was enthroned, he followed the princely establishment and was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works, concurrently Administrator of Linhuai; his generalship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor Liu Yu was placed on the throne, Xiao followed his household and became Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works while also serving as Administrator of Linhuai, retaining his general's title.

sentences.zh: 轉太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the Grand Marshal's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the staff of the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 齊臺建，爲吏部郎。

translations.literal: When the Qi regency was established, he became Director of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Qi regency was set up, he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽位，斆以祖母久疾連年，臺閣之職，永廢溫凊，啓乞自解。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Xiao, because his grandmother had been ill for years, had forever neglected the warmth and coolness of proper attendance at court offices, and submitted a request to resign of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founding Emperor acceded, Xiao petitioned to resign, explaining that his grandmother had been ill for years and that his duties at court had long kept him from fulfilling the daily attentions owed to her.

sentences.zh: 初，宋明帝勑斆出繼從叔愻，爲從祖淳後。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Ming of Song had ordered Xiao to leave his own line and succeed his father's younger cousin Min, becoming heir to his great-uncle Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Ming of Song had commanded Xiao to leave his birth family and succeed his father's younger cousin Jiang Min as heir to his great-uncle Jiang Chun.

sentences.zh: 於是僕射王儉啓：「禮無後小宗之文，近世緣情，皆由父祖之命，未有旣孤之後，出繼宗族也。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Left Vice Premier Wang Jian submitted: "The rites contain no provision for making an heir of a lesser lineage; in recent times, following human feeling, all such cases have been by the command of father or grandfather—there has never been leaving one's own clan after one is already orphaned.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wang Jian, Vice Premier of the Left, memorialized: "The rites provide no precedent for adopting an heir into a lesser lineage; in recent practice such arrangements have followed affection and always rested on a father's or grandfather's command—never on leaving one's own clan after one is already orphaned.

sentences.zh: 雖復臣子一揆，而義非天屬。

translations.literal: Although minister and son are in one category, the bond is not that of Heaven's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Although the roles of minister and son may look alike, the bond is not one ordained by Heaven's kinship.

sentences.zh: 江忠簡胤嗣所寄，唯斆一人，傍無眷屬。

translations.literal: The line of loyal and simple Jiang Zhongjian had only Xiao to carry on its succession, with no collateral kin beside him.
translations.idiomatic: The line of the loyal and upright Jiang Zhongjian had placed its hopes for succession solely in Xiao, with no other close kin at his side.

sentences.zh: 斆宜還本。

translations.literal: Xiao ought to return to his original family.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao should be restored to his birth family.

sentences.zh: 若不欲江愻絕後，可以斆小兒繼愻爲孫。

translations.literal: If one does not wish Jiang Min's line to end, Xiao's young son may succeed Min as grandson.
translations.idiomatic: If the court does not wish Jiang Min's line to die out, Xiao's young son may be made Min's grandson and heir.

sentences.zh: 」尚書參議，謂「間世立後，禮無其文。

translations.literal: " The Masters of Writing deliberated and said: "Establishing an heir across generations has no textual basis in the rites.
translations.idiomatic: " The Masters of Writing deliberated and ruled that "establishing an heir across generations has no basis in the canonical rites.

sentences.zh: 荀顗無子立孫，墜禮之始。

translations.literal: When Xun Yi, having no son, established a grandson as heir, that was the beginning of the rites' fall.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun Yi, lacking a son, made his grandson his heir, that marked the beginning of the rites' decline.

sentences.zh: 何琦又立此論，義無所據」。

translations.literal: He Qi again set forth this argument, which has no basis in right principle."
translations.idiomatic: He Qi's revival of this argument likewise rests on no valid principle."

sentences.zh: 於是斆還本家，詔使自量立後者。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiao returned to his original family, and an edict ordered him to decide for himself whom to establish as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao was therefore restored to his birth family, and an edict directed him to choose his own heir.

sentences.zh: 出爲寧朔將軍、豫章內史，還除太子中庶子，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Interior Minister of Yuzhang; on return he was appointed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and Interior Minister of Yuzhang; on returning to court he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent while also holding the rank of General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 未拜，門客通贓利，世祖遣信撿覈，斆藏此客而躬自引咎，上甚有怪色。

translations.literal: Before he took up the appointment, a house guest had trafficked in illicit profit; Emperor Wu sent an envoy to investigate; Xiao concealed the guest and personally accepted blame; the emperor's expression was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume the post, a retainer had been taking bribes; Emperor Wu sent agents to investigate; Xiao hid the man and took the blame upon himself, and the emperor looked greatly displeased.

sentences.zh: 王儉從容啓上曰：「江斆若能治郡，此便是具美耳。

translations.literal: Wang Jian calmly reported to the emperor: "If Jiang Xiao can govern a commandery, this in itself is complete excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian calmly said to the emperor, "If Jiang Xiao can govern a commandery well, that alone would be excellence enough.

sentences.zh: 」上意乃釋。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mind was then released.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 永明初，仍爲豫章王太尉諮議，領錄事，遷南郡王友，竟陵王司徒司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongming era he again served as Adviser to the Grand Marshal for Prince Yuzhang, concurrently Recorder, was transferred to Companion of Prince Nanjun, and became Secretary on the Minister of Works staff for Prince Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongming reign he again served Prince Yuzhang as Adviser to the Grand Marshal and Recorder, then became Companion to Prince Nanjun and Secretary on the staff of Prince Jingling of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 斆好文辭，圍棊第五品，爲朝貴中最。

translations.literal: Xiao loved literary composition; in weiqi he was fifth rank, the highest among court nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao loved literature and excelled at weiqi, ranked fifth class—the best among the court elite.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，領本州中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and concurrently Director of Selection for his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and also served as provincial Director of Selection for his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 司徒左長史，中正如故。

translations.literal: Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works; his directorship of selection was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He became Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works while retaining his post as Director of Selection.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷五兵尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Minister of the Five Armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongming he was made Minister of the Five Armies.

sentences.zh: 明年，出爲輔國將軍、東海太守，加秩中二千石，行南徐州事。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Donghai, with salary raised to two thousand shi middle grade, acting for Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent out as General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Donghai, with rank raised to two thousand shi (middle grade), and was placed in charge of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，卒，年四十四。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he died, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jianwu era he died at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 遺令儉約葬，不受賻贈。

translations.literal: His final instructions ordered a frugal burial and that no funeral gifts be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In his final instructions he called for a simple burial and refused any funeral gifts from the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔賻錢三萬，布百匹。

translations.literal: An edict granted funeral gifts of thirty thousand cash and a hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered thirty thousand cash and a hundred bolts of cloth as funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 子蒨啓遵斆令，讓不受。

translations.literal: His son Qian reported that he was following Xiao's command and declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiang Qian reported that he was obeying Xiao's wishes and declined the gifts.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「斆貽厥之訓，送終以儉，立言歸善，益有嘉傷，可從所請。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Xiao left instructions to his descendants, saw the end with frugality, and in his words returned to goodness—this increases what is worthy of praise and mourning; his request may be granted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Xiao bequeathed moral instruction to his heirs, arranged his own end with restraint, and in his words turned toward what is good—this only deepens what is admirable and lamentable; let his request be granted.

sentences.zh: 」贈散騎常侍、太常，謚曰敬子。

translations.literal: " He was posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Scattershot Cavalry and Minister of Ceremonies; his posthumous title was Respectful Son.
translations.idiomatic: " He was posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Scattershot Cavalry and Minister of Ceremonies, with the posthumous title Respectful Son.

sentences.zh: 何昌字儼望，廬江灊人也。

translations.literal: He Chang, courtesy name Yiwang, was a man of Qian in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Chang, whose courtesy name was Yiwang, came from Qian in Lujiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖叔度，吳郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shudu was Administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather He Shudu served as Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父佟之，太常。

translations.literal: His father Tongzhi was Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His father He Tongzhi was Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 昌少而淹厚，爲伯父司空尚之所遇。

translations.literal: Chang from youth was deep and substantial and was favored by his uncle, the Minister of Works Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chang was thoughtful and steady, and won the favor of his uncle He Shangzhi, who served as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 宋建安王休仁爲揚州，辟昌州主簿。

translations.literal: In Song, Prince Jian'an Xiuren was in charge of Yang province and invited Chang as provincial Master of Records.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jian'an of Xiuren held Yang Province in the Song, he recruited Chang as provincial Master of Records.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒行參軍，太傅五官，司徒東閤祭酒，尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Adjutant of the Minister of Works, Fifth Officer of the Grand Tutor, Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Minister of Works, and Attendant of the Bureau of Rites in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Acting Adjutant on the Minister of Works staff, Fifth Officer of the Grand Tutor, Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Minister of Works, and Attendant of the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 建平王景素爲征北南徐州，昌又爲府主簿，以夙素見重。

translations.literal: Prince Jianping Jingsu was Northern Expedition Commander for Southern Xuzhou; Chang again served as princely Master of Records and was valued for his long-standing integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jianping of Jingsu served as Northern Expedition Commander for Southern Xuzhou, Chang again became his Master of Records and was esteemed for his longstanding integrity.

sentences.zh: 母老求祿，出爲湘東太守，加秩千石。

translations.literal: His mother was aged and he sought an office with salary; he went out as Administrator of Xiangdong, with rank raised to one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was elderly he sought a salaried post and was sent out as Administrator of Xiangdong, with rank raised to one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 爲太祖驃騎功曹。

translations.literal: He became Merit Officer on the Rapid Cavalry staff of the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He later served the Founding Emperor as Merit Officer on his Rapid Cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 昌在郡，景素被誅，昌痛之。

translations.literal: While Chang was in the commandery, Jingsu was executed; Chang grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: While Chang was still in the commandery, Jingsu was put to death, and Chang was stricken with grief.

sentences.zh: 至是啓太祖曰：

translations.literal: At this time he submitted a memorial to the Founding Emperor, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted this memorial to the Founding Emperor:

sentences.zh: 伏尋故建平王，因心自遠，忠孝基性，徽和之譽，早布國言，勝素之情，夙洽民聽。

translations.literal: I humbly consider the late Prince Jianping: by nature he kept himself aloof, with loyalty and filial piety as the foundation of his character; his reputation for harmony and excellence was early spread in the state's words, and his surpassing integrity was long known to the people's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully recall the late Prince Jianping: by nature he held himself apart from intrigue, with loyalty and filial piety at the core of his character; his reputation for grace and integrity had long been known throughout the realm, and his surpassing purity was familiar to all who heard of him.

sentences.zh: 世祖綢繆，太宗眷異，朝中貴人，野外賤士，雖聞見有殊，誰不悉斯事者？

translations.literal: The Former Emperor was intimate with him, the Founding Emperor regarded him with special favor; whether court nobles or humble men in the wilds, though what they heard and saw differed, who did not know this affair?
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor treated him with affection, and the Founding Emperor regarded him with special favor; whether court nobles or commoners in the countryside, though their knowledge differed in detail, who did not know what had happened?

sentences.zh: 元徽之間，政關羣小，構扇異端，共令傾覆。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhui era government fell into the hands of petty men, who stirred up heterodox schemes and together brought about his overthrow.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhui era power passed into the hands of petty men, who stirred up factional intrigue and together brought about his ruin.

sentences.zh: 慇懃之非，古人所悼，況蒼梧將季，能無衒惑。

translations.literal: Offenses born of earnest zeal are what the ancients lamented; how much more when Cangwu was nearing its end could there fail to be delusion and confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Misdeeds born of misguided zeal are what the ancients mourned; how much more, when the house of Cangwu was nearing its fall, could there fail to be delusion and unrest.

sentences.zh: 一年之中，藉者再三，有必巔之危，無蹔立之安，行路寒心，往來跼蹐。

translations.literal: Within a single year calamities struck again and again; there was the peril of certain toppling, no moment's standing peace; travelers felt their hearts turn cold, and comings and goings were cramped and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single year disaster struck again and again; he faced the constant threat of ruin and never a moment's security; travelers shuddered on the road, and all who passed by went in fear and constraint.

sentences.zh: 而王夷慮坦然，委之天命，惟謙惟敬，專誠奉國，閨無執戟之衞，門闕衣介之夫，此五尺童子所見，不假闊曲言也。

translations.literal: Yet the prince, with mind level and open, entrusted himself to Heaven's mandate, was only humble and reverent, devoted his sincerity to serving the state; his inner quarters had no guards with halberds, his gates lacked men in armor—this a child of five feet could see, without need of broad or circuitous words.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the prince remained serene in spirit, entrusted himself to fate, and was humble and reverent in serving the state with undivided loyalty; his inner quarters had no halberd-bearing guards, his gates no armored retainers—what any child could see, without need of elaborate explanation.

sentences.zh: 一淪疑似，身名頓滅，冤結淵泉，酷貫穹昊。

translations.literal: Once he fell into suspicion, body and name were suddenly extinguished; grievance knotted in the deep springs, cruelty pierced the vaulted sky.
translations.idiomatic: Once he fell under suspicion, his life and reputation were destroyed at a stroke; injustice sank to the depths of the underworld, and cruelty reached to the heavens.

sentences.zh: 時經隆替，歲改三元，曠蕩之惠亟申，被枉之澤未流。

translations.literal: Time has passed through rise and fall; years have turned with the three first days; the broad and generous favor has been repeatedly proclaimed, yet the grace for the wrongly treated has not flowed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasties have risen and fallen, years have turned with each new reign, and broad amnesties have been proclaimed again and again—yet the grace owed to the wronged has never reached him.

sentences.zh: 俱沐溫光，獨酸霜露。

translations.literal: All alike bathe in warm light; he alone tastes the bitterness of frost and dew.
translations.idiomatic: All others bask in the emperor's warmth, while he alone suffers the bitterness of frost and dew.

sentences.zh: 明公鋪天地之施，散雲雨之潤，物無巨細，咸被慶渥。

translations.literal: Your Excellency spreads Heaven and Earth's bounty, disperses the moisture of clouds and rain; nothing, great or small, fails to receive joyous favor.
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency spreads bounty as wide as Heaven and Earth and showers grace like rain on the land; nothing, great or small, fails to share in your blessings.

sentences.zh: 若今日不蒙照滌，則爲萬代冤魂。

translations.literal: If today he does not receive your illuminating cleansing, he will become a wronged ghost for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: If he is not cleared by your grace today, he will remain a wronged spirit for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 昌非敢慕慷慨之士，激揚當世，實義切於心，痛入骨髓。

translations.literal: Chang does not dare to emulate men of generous spirit who rouse their own age; in truth righteousness cuts to the heart, and pain enters the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: I do not presume to imitate the heroes who stir their age with bold words; my plea springs from duty that cuts to the heart and grief that reaches the bone.

sentences.zh: 瀝腸紓憤，仰希神照，辯明枉直，亮王素行，使還名帝籍，歸靈舊塋，死而不泯，豈忘德於黃壚。

translations.literal: Pouring out my entrails to release anger, I look up hoping for divine illumination, to distinguish wrong from right, to display the prince's plain conduct, to restore his name to the imperial registers, return his spirit to the old mound—though dead, not extinguished; how could I forget virtue in the yellow earth?
translations.idiomatic: I pour out my heart to ease this anguish and look up to your enlightened judgment, asking only that wrong be distinguished from right, that the prince's true character be revealed, that his name be restored to the imperial registers and his spirit to his ancestral tomb—so that though dead he may not be forgotten, and I may not fail in gratitude even from the yellow earth of the grave.

sentences.zh: 分軀碎首，不足上謝。

translations.literal: To split my body and shatter my head would not suffice to repay you above.
translations.idiomatic: Even to give my body and life would not be thanks enough.

sentences.zh: 又與司空褚淵書曰：

translations.literal: He also wrote a letter to the Minister of Works Chu Yuan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Chu Yuan, Minister of Works, as follows:

sentences.zh: 天下之可哀者有數，而埋冤於黃泉者爲甚焉。

translations.literal: Among the world's lamentable things there are several, but burying grievance in the Yellow Springs is the gravest.
translations.idiomatic: The world holds many causes for sorrow, but none is worse than burying a man's injustice in the grave.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 百年之壽，同於朝露，揮忽去留，寧足道哉！

translations.literal: A lifespan of a hundred years is like morning dew; sudden coming and going—how could it be worth speaking of!
translations.idiomatic: A lifetime of a hundred years is no more than morning dew; one's coming and going are swift—what is there to boast of?

sentences.zh: 政欲闔棺之日，不隕令名，竹帛傳芳烈，鐘石紀清英。

translations.literal: What one truly desires is that on the day the coffin is closed one's fair name not fall, that silk and bamboo transmit one's fragrant deeds, that bells and stones record one's pure excellence.
translations.idiomatic: What men truly desire is that when the coffin lid closes their good name may not fall, that silk and bamboo may carry their virtue abroad, and that bells and stone inscriptions may preserve their excellence.

sentences.zh: 是以昔賢甘心於死所者也。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages of old were content to die where they must.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the worthies of old were willing to die where they stood.

sentences.zh: 若懷忠抱義，而負枉冥冥之下，時主未之矜，卿相不爲言，良史濡翰，將被以惡名，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: If one embraces loyalty and holds to righteousness, yet bears wrong in the darkness below, the ruler of the time does not pity him, ministers and premiers do not speak for him, and the good historian, brush wet, will clothe him in an evil name—how could it not be painful!
translations.idiomatic: If a man who cherishes loyalty and righteousness is wronged in the grave, and the ruler shows him no mercy, and ministers do not speak for him, and the historian's brush records only a foul name—how could that not be unbearable!

sentences.zh: 豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: How could it not be painful!
translations.idiomatic: How could it not be unbearable!

sentences.zh: 竊尋故建平王，地屬親賢，德居宗望，道心惟沖，睿性天峻。

translations.literal: I privately consider the late Prince Jianping: in station he belonged to the imperial kin and worthies, in virtue he stood at the head of the clan's hopes, his Dao-mind was only pure, his keen nature Heaven-high and stern.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect on the late Prince Jianping: by birth he was of the imperial kin and the worthiest of princes, by virtue he stood foremost among the clan, his mind was pure and his nature lofty and keen.

sentences.zh: 散情風雲，不以塵務嬰衿，明發懷古，惟以琴書娛志。

translations.literal: He scattered his feelings among wind and clouds, did not let dusty affairs bind his collar; at dawn he cherished antiquity, and only with zither and books amused his will.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his heart to wind and clouds, would not let worldly affairs trouble his breast, rose at dawn to muse on antiquity, and found his joy only in zither and books.

sentences.zh: 言忠孝，行惇慎，二公之所深鑒也。

translations.literal: In speech loyalty and filial piety, in conduct honest caution—this both of you have deeply discerned.
translations.idiomatic: His words spoke of loyalty and filial piety, his conduct was sincere and cautious—both of you know this well.

sentences.zh: 前者阮、楊連黨，搆此紛紜，雖被明於朝貴，愈結怨於羣醜。

translations.literal: Earlier Ruan and Yang formed a faction and stirred up this turmoil; though the prince was cleared before the court nobles, he only bound grievance more tightly among the wicked throng.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruan and Yang formed their faction and stirred up this turmoil, though the prince was cleared in the eyes of the court, he only earned deeper hatred from the villainous crowd.

sentences.zh: 覘察繼蹤，疑防重著，小人在朝，詩史所歎，

translations.literal: Spying and watching followed in his tracks, suspicion and guard redoubled; petty men in court—what the Odes and Histories lament,
translations.idiomatic: Spies watched his every move, suspicion and guard redoubled upon him; petty men held sway at court—the very thing the Odes and Histories lament,

sentences.zh: 〈少一句〉

translations.literal: 〈One sentence missing in the source text.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Lacuna: one sentence is missing in the source text.〉

sentences.zh: 清識飲涕。

translations.literal: men of clear insight drank tears.
translations.idiomatic: and men of clear insight wept.

sentences.zh: 王每永言終日，氣淚交橫。

translations.literal: The prince each day spoke at length until day's end, breath and tears crossing.
translations.idiomatic: The prince would speak at length all day, his breath catching and tears streaming.

sentences.zh: 旣推信以期物，故日去其備衞，朱門蕭條，示存典刑而已。

translations.literal: Having extended trust to win others' hearts, he therefore daily reduced his guards; the vermilion gate grew desolate, showing only that the ritual punishments still existed.
translations.idiomatic: Because he extended trust to win men's hearts, he daily reduced his guards; his vermilion gates grew bare, showing only that he still upheld the proper rites.

sentences.zh: 求解徐州，以避北門要任，苦乞會稽，貪處東甌閑務，此竝彰於事迹。

translations.literal: He sought release from Xuzhou to avoid the crucial post at the northern gate; he bitterly begged for Kuaiji, eager to dwell in the idle duties of eastern Yong—this all is manifest in the record of deeds.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be relieved of Xuzhou to avoid a key post at the capital's northern gate, and pleaded earnestly for Kuaiji, longing for the quiet duties of the eastern frontier—all this is clear from the record of his conduct.

sentences.zh: 與公道味相求，期心有素，方共經營家國，劬勞王室，何圖時不我與，契闊屯昏，忠誠弗亮，罹此百殃。

translations.literal: With Your Lordship he sought kindred taste, their hearts long bound in trust, just then together managing state and clan, toiling for the royal house—who thought the times would not grant him, that parting in hardship and darkness would come, that loyalty would not shine forth, and he would suffer these hundred calamities.
translations.idiomatic: He sought your company as a kindred spirit, and your hearts had long been joined in trust; you were just then together planning for state and throne, laboring for the royal house—who could have foreseen that time would fail him, that separation and darkness would come, that his loyalty would go unrecognized, and that he would suffer every calamity?

sentences.zh: 歲朔亟流，已經四載。

translations.literal: Years and new years swiftly flow; already four years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: Years have passed swiftly; four years have already gone by.

sentences.zh: 皇命惟新，人沾天澤，而幽然深酷。

translations.literal: The imperial mandate is wholly new, men bathe in Heaven's grace, yet he remains darkly deep in bitterness.
translations.idiomatic: A new reign has begun and all men share the emperor's grace, yet he remains sunk in deepest sorrow.

sentences.zh: 未蒙照明。

translations.literal: He has not received illuminating grace.
translations.idiomatic: He has not yet received the light of imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 封殯卑雜，窮魂莫寄，昭穆不序，松柏無行。

translations.literal: His sealing and burial were low and disorderly, his destitute spirit has nowhere to rest, the ancestral sequence is not in order, pine and cypress stand in no rows.
translations.idiomatic: His burial was mean and disorderly, his spirit has nowhere to rest, the ancestral order is unsettled, and no rows of pine and cypress mark his tomb.

sentences.zh: 事傷行路，痛結幽顯。

translations.literal: The affair wounds travelers on the road; grief knots the hidden and the manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The matter wounds all who pass on the road; grief binds the living and the dead.

sentences.zh: 吾等叩心泣血，實有望於聖時。

translations.literal: We knock our hearts and weep blood; we truly place hope in this sage era.
translations.idiomatic: We beat our breasts and weep blood, and truly place our hope in this enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 公以德佐世，欲物得其所，豈可令建平王枉直不分邪？

translations.literal: Your Lordship, with virtue assisting the age, wishes all things to obtain their proper place—how could you let Prince Jianping's wrong and right go undistinguished?
translations.idiomatic: You, who assist the age with virtue and wish every man his due—how can you allow Prince Jianping's innocence and guilt to remain undistinguished?

sentences.zh: 田叔不言梁事，袁絲諫止淮南，以兩國舋禍，尚回帝意，豈非親親之義，寧從敦厚。

translations.literal: Tian Shu did not speak of Liang's affair; Yuan Si admonished and stopped Huainan; because the two states raised calamity, they still turned back the emperor's mind—was this not the meaning of cherishing kin, preferring generous thickness?
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shu held his tongue on the affair of Liang; Yuan Si admonished the emperor and stayed the revolt of Huainan; though both realms had courted disaster, they still turned the emperor's heart—was this not the spirit of cherishing one's kin and choosing clemency over severity?

sentences.zh: 而今疑似未辨，爲世大戮。

translations.literal: Yet now suspicion is not yet distinguished, and he suffers the great punishment of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now his guilt remains undistinguished, and he has suffered the greatest punishment of the age.

sentences.zh: 若使王心迹得申，亦示海內理冤枉，明是非。

translations.literal: If the prince's mind and tracks could be expressed, it would also show the realm how to set right wrongs and clarify right from wrong.
translations.idiomatic: If the prince's true intentions could be made known, it would show the realm how to right wrongs and distinguish truth from falsehood.

sentences.zh: 夫存亡國，繼絕世，周漢之通典，有國之所急也。

translations.literal: To preserve a state on the verge of perishing and continue a line on the verge of ending is the common canon of Zhou and Han—what a state holding the realm most urgently needs.
translations.idiomatic: To preserve a state on the brink of ruin and continue a line on the verge of extinction was the common duty of Zhou and Han—what any realm most urgently requires.

sentences.zh: 昔叔向之理，恃祁大夫而獲亮，戾太子之冤，資車丞相而見察。

translations.literal: Of old Shu Xiang's case was cleared relying on Grandee Qi; the wrong of Crown Prince Li was discerned with the aid of Chancellor Che.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Shu Xiang's cause was cleared through Grandee Qi; the injustice done to Crown Prince Li was recognized with the help of Chancellor Che.

sentences.zh: 幽靈有知，豈不眷眷於明顧？

translations.literal: If the hidden spirits have knowledge, would they not look back with longing on bright regard?
translations.idiomatic: If the spirits have understanding, would they not look back with longing on your enlightened regard?

sentences.zh: 碎首抽脅，自謂不殞。

translations.literal: To shatter my head and tear my ribs—I deem it no ruin.
translations.idiomatic: To shatter my head and tear my limbs—I would count it no loss.

sentences.zh: 淵答曰：「追風古人，良以嘉歎。

translations.literal: Yuan replied: "Chasing the wind of the ancients—truly worthy of praise and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan replied, "Your zeal rivals that of the ancients, and I cannot but admire it.

sentences.zh: 但事旣昭晦，理有逆從。

translations.literal: But the affair is already bright and dark; principle has what must be followed and what must be opposed.
translations.idiomatic: But the matter is already settled in light and shadow, and principle admits no reversal.

sentences.zh: 建平初阻，元徽未悖，專欲委咎阮、楊，彌所致疑。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianping there was obstruction; in Yuanhui there was not yet rebellion—one wished solely to lay blame on Ruan and Yang, which only increased the suspicion incurred.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianping there was obstruction, and in Yuanhui there was not yet open rebellion—the aim was solely to lay blame on Ruan and Yang, which only deepened the suspicion against the prince.

sentences.zh: 于時正亦謬參此機，若審如高論，其愧特深。

translations.literal: At that time I too wrongly took part in this scheme; if it is truly as your lofty argument says, my shame is especially deep."
translations.idiomatic: At that time I too was wrongly involved in this affair; if your noble argument is correct, my shame is all the deeper."

sentences.zh: 」太祖嘉其義，轉爲記室，遷司徒左西、太尉戶曹屬，中書郎，王儉衞軍長史。

translations.literal: " The Founding Emperor praised his righteousness, transferred him to be Recorder, promoted him to Western Left of the Minister of Works, Attendant of the Household Bureau on the Grand Marshal's staff, Palace Secretariat Attendant, and Chief Clerk on Wang Jian's Guard staff.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor praised his integrity and made him Recorder, then promoted him through Western Left of the Minister of Works, Attendant of the Household Bureau on the Grand Marshal's staff, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Chief Clerk on Wang Jian's Guard staff.

sentences.zh: 儉謂昌曰：「後任朝事者，非卿而誰？」

translations.literal: Jian said to Chang: "He who will later bear the court's affairs—if not you, then who?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian told him, "Who but you will one day bear the weight of the court's affairs?"

sentences.zh: 永明元年，竟陵王子良表置友、學官，以昌爲竟陵王文學，以清信相得，意好甚厚。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming, Prince Jingling of Ziliang memorialized to establish Companions and Academy officers; Chang was made Literary Scholar for Prince Jingling; through purity and trust they won each other, and their affection was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming, Prince Jingling of Ziliang petitioned to establish Companions and Academy officers; Chang was made Literary Scholar to the prince, and they drew together in purity and trust with deep mutual affection.

sentences.zh: 轉揚州別駕，豫章王又善之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Vice Administrator of Yang province; Prince Yuzhang also favored him.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Administrator of Yang Province, and Prince Yuzhang also held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 遷太子中庶子，出爲臨川內史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and went out as Interior Minister of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and sent out as Interior Minister of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 除廬陵王中軍長史，未拜，復爲太子中庶子，領屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk on the Central Army staff of Prince Luling but did not accept; he again became Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Commandant of the Garrison Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chief Clerk on Prince Luling's Central Army staff but did not take up the post; he again became Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and also Commandant of the Garrison Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部郎，轉侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Personnel and then to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Bureau of Personnel and then Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 臨海王昭秀爲荊州，以昌爲西中郎長史、輔國將軍、南郡太守，行荊州事。

translations.literal: Prince Linhai Zhaoxiu was in charge of Jing province; Chang was made Chief Clerk of the Western Central Commandant, General Who Assists the State, and Administrator of Nanjun, acting for Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Linhai of Zhaoxiu held Jing Province, Chang was made his Chief Clerk, General Who Assists the State, and Administrator of Nanjun, with charge of Jing Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 明帝遣徐玄慶西上害蕃鎮諸王，玄慶至荊州，欲以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent Xu Xuanqing west to harm the feudatory princes at the frontier; Xuanqing reached Jing province and wished to act as expedience required.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Xu Xuanqing west to eliminate the feudatory princes; when Xuanqing reached Jing Province he intended to act on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 昌曰：「僕受朝廷意寄，翼輔外蕃，何容以殿下付君一介之使。

translations.literal: Chang said: "I have received the court's trust and am to assist the outer feudatory—how could I hand over Your Highness to a single envoy of yours?
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "I have received the court's trust to assist the frontier princes—how could I deliver Your Highness into the hands of a single envoy?

sentences.zh: 若朝廷必須殿下還，當更聽後旨。

translations.literal: If the court truly requires Your Highness to return, we should await further orders."
translations.idiomatic: If the court truly requires Your Highness to return to the capital, we must await further imperial orders."

sentences.zh: 」昭秀以此得還京師。

translations.literal: " Zhaoxiu thereby was able to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to this, Zhaoxiu was able to return safely to the capital.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，爲侍中，領長水校尉，轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he became Palace Attendant and concurrently Commandant of the Long River, then Minister of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu he was made Palace Attendant and Commandant of the Long River, then Minister of the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 復爲侍中，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He again became Palace Attendant and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Palace Attendant and General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died.

sentences.zh: 年五十一。

translations.literal: He was fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-one years old.

sentences.zh: 贈太常，謚簡子。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies; his posthumous title was Simple Son.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Ceremonies, with the posthumous title Simple Son.

sentences.zh: 昌不雜交遊，通和汎愛。

translations.literal: Chang did not mix in social rounds; he was universally harmonious and broadly loving.
translations.idiomatic: Chang did not cultivate a wide circle of associates, yet he was universally gentle and generous in spirit.

sentences.zh: 歷郡皆清白，士君子多稱之。

translations.literal: In every commandery he served he was pure and clean; gentlemen widely praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In every commandery he served he maintained a spotless record, and men of worth widely praised him.

sentences.zh: 謝𤅢字義潔，陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Xie Yao, courtesy name Yijie, was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yao, whose courtesy name was Yijie, came from Yangxia in Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖弘微，宋太常。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hongwei was Minister of Ceremonies in Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xie Hongwei served as Minister of Ceremonies in the Song.

sentences.zh: 父莊，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Zhuang was Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie Zhuang was Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 𤅢四兄颺、朏、顥、嵷，世謂謝莊名兒爲風、月、景、山、水。

translations.literal: Yao had four elder brothers Yang, Tiao, Hao, and Chong; the age called Xie Zhuang's naming of his sons Wind, Moon, Scenery, Mountain, and Water.
translations.idiomatic: Yao had four elder brothers—Yang, Tiao, Hao, and Chong—and the world said that Xie Zhuang had named his sons Wind, Moon, Scenery, Mountain, and Water.

sentences.zh: 顥字仁悠，少簡靜。

translations.literal: Hao, courtesy name Renyou, from youth was simple and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, whose courtesy name was Renyou, was from youth simple and reserved.

sentences.zh: 解褐祕書郎，累至太祖驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: On leaving the sackcloth he became Secretary Attendant and rose to Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he became Secretary Attendant and rose to Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 建元初，爲吏部郎，至太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he was Director of the Bureau of Personnel, reaching Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the Grand Marshal's staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianyuan he was Director of the Bureau of Personnel and eventually Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the Grand Marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 永明初，高選友、學，以顥爲竟陵王友。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming, in the high selection of Companions and scholars, Hao was made Companion to Prince Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongming, in the rigorous selection of princely Companions and scholars, Hao was made Companion to Prince Jingling.

sentences.zh: 至北中郎長史。

translations.literal: He reached Chief Clerk of the Northern Central Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Chief Clerk of the Northern Central Commandant.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 𤅢年七歲，王彧見而異之，言於宋孝武，孝武召見於稠人廣衆之中，𤅢舉動閑詳，應對合旨，帝甚悅。

translations.literal: At age seven Yao was seen by Wang Yu and considered extraordinary; Yu spoke of him to Emperor Xiaowu of Song; Xiaowu summoned him for audience in a dense crowd; Yao's bearing was leisurely and careful, his replies accorded with intent, and the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao was seven, Wang Yu saw him and was struck by his quality; he spoke of him to Emperor Xiaowu of Song, who summoned the boy before a great crowd; Yao's bearing was composed and his answers apt, and the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 詔尚公主，值景和敗，事寢。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to marry a princess; it happened that Jinghe was overthrown and the matter lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to marry an imperial princess, but when Liu Ziye (Emperor Jinghe) fell the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 僕射褚淵聞𤅢年少清正不惡，以女結婚，厚爲資送。

translations.literal: Vice Premier Chu Yuan heard that Yao in youth was pure, upright, and not ill-natured, and gave him his daughter in marriage with a generous dowry.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Premier Chu Yuan heard that the young Yao was pure and upright, gave him his daughter in marriage, and provided a generous dowry.

sentences.zh: 解褐車騎行參軍，遷祕書郎，司徒祭酒，丹陽丞，撫軍功曹。

translations.literal: On leaving the sackcloth he was Acting Adjutant on the Chariots and Cavalry staff, transferred to Secretary Attendant, Libationer of the Minister of Works, Assistant Magistrate of Danyang, and Merit Officer of the Pacification Army.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he was Acting Adjutant on the Chariots and Cavalry staff, then Secretary Attendant, Libationer of the Minister of Works, Assistant Magistrate of Danyang, and Merit Officer of the Pacification Army.

sentences.zh: 世祖爲中軍，引爲記室。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was Central Army Commander he brought him in as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu served as Central Army Commander he took Yao on as Recorder.

sentences.zh: 齊臺建，遷太子中舍人。

translations.literal: When the Qi regency was established he was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regency was established he was made Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 建元初，轉桂陽王友。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he was transferred to Companion of Prince Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianyuan he became Companion to Prince Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 以母老須養，出爲安成內史。

translations.literal: Because his mother was aged and needed support, he went out as Interior Minister of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was elderly and needed care, he was sent out as Interior Minister of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 還爲中書郎。

translations.literal: On return he became Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was made Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 衞軍王儉引爲長史，雅相禮遇。

translations.literal: General of the Guard Wang Jian brought him in as Chief Clerk and treated him with elegant courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, General of the Guard, took him on as Chief Clerk and treated him with marked esteem.

sentences.zh: 除黃門郎，兼掌吏部。

translations.literal: He was appointed Yellow Gate Attendant and concurrently managed the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate and also placed in charge of the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尋轉太子中庶子，領驍騎將軍，轉長兼侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry, then Chief Clerk and concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and General of Valiant Cavalry, then Chief Clerk and concurrently Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 𤅢以晨昏有廢，固辭不受。

translations.literal: Yao, because morning and evening attendance would be neglected, firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yao declined firmly, saying that the post would keep him from attending his parents morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 世祖勑令速拜，別停朝直。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu ordered him to accept quickly and separately suspended his court attendance duty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu ordered him to accept at once and exempted him from regular court attendance.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒左長史，出爲吳興太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works and went out as Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works and sent out as Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 長城縣民盧道優家遭劫，誣同縣殷孝悌等四人爲劫，𤅢收付縣獄考正。

translations.literal: Lu Daoyou, a commoner of Changcheng county, suffered robbery at home and falsely accused four men of the same county, including Yin Xiaoti, as robbers; Yao took them and handed them to the county prison for examination.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Daoyou of Changcheng County was robbed at home, he falsely accused Yin Xiaoti and three other men from the same county; Yao had them arrested and sent to the county prison for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 孝悌母駱詣登聞訴稱孝悌爲道優所誹謗，橫劾爲劫，一百七十三人連名保徵，在所不爲申理。

translations.literal: Xiaoti's mother Luo went to the Petition Office and complained that Xiaoti had been slandered by Daoyou and falsely charged as a robber; one hundred seventy-three persons signed a joint guarantee petition, but the local office did not grant redress.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoti's mother, Lady Luo, petitioned at the Petition Office, claiming her son had been slandered by Daoyou and falsely charged with robbery; one hundred seventy-three people signed a joint guarantee, but the local authorities refused to act.

sentences.zh: 𤅢聞孝悌母訴，乃啓建康獄覆，道優理窮款首，依法斬刑。

translations.literal: When Yao heard of Xiaoti's mother's complaint, he submitted for a retrial at the Jiankang prison; Daoyou, his case exhausted, confessed, and was beheaded according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao heard of the mother's petition, he ordered a retrial at the Jiankang prison; Daoyou, his case exhausted, confessed and was beheaded according to law.

sentences.zh: 有司奏免𤅢官。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized to dismiss Yao from office.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices memorialized for Yao's dismissal.

sentences.zh: 又使典藥吏煮湯，失火，燒郡外齋南廂屋五閒。

translations.literal: He also had a pharmacy clerk boil medicine; fire broke out and burned five bays of the southern wing of the outer quarters of the commandery residence.
translations.idiomatic: He also had a pharmacy clerk boil medicine; a fire broke out and burned five bays of the southern wing of the commandery's outer quarters.

sentences.zh: 又輙鞭除身，爲有司所奏，詔竝贖論。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly flogged his personal attendants and was reported by the responsible offices; an edict pardoned all charges by ransom.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly flogged his personal attendants and was reported to the throne; an edict pardoned all charges.

sentences.zh: 在郡稱爲美績。

translations.literal: In the commandery he was praised for fine achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he was praised for excellent administration.

sentences.zh: 母喪去官。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office upon his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 服闋，爲吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became Minister of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made Minister of the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 高宗廢鬱林，領兵入殿，左右驚走報𤅢。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao deposed the Prince of Yulin and led troops into the palace; attendants fled in alarm to report to Yao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao deposed the Prince of Yulin and led troops into the palace, attendants fled in alarm to report to Yao.

sentences.zh: 與客圍棊，每下子，輙云「其當有意」。

translations.literal: He was playing weiqi with a guest; with each stone placed he would say, "There must be some intent in this."
translations.idiomatic: He was playing weiqi with a guest and with each move would say, "They must have some purpose in this."

sentences.zh: 竟局，乃還齋卧，竟不問外事也。

translations.literal: When the game ended he returned to his quarters to sleep and never inquired into outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the game ended he returned to his quarters to sleep and never asked about outside affairs.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，𤅢又屬疾不視事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Yao again pleaded illness and did not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming acceded, Yao again pleaded illness and declined to attend to affairs.

sentences.zh: 後上讌會，功臣上酒，尚書令王晏等興席，𤅢獨不起，曰：「陛下受命，應天從民，王晏妄叨天功以爲己力。

translations.literal: Later at a court banquet, when meritorious ministers offered wine, Minister of Works Wang Yan and others rose from their seats; Yao alone did not rise and said: "Your Majesty received the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people—Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own power.
translations.idiomatic: Later at a court banquet, when meritorious ministers offered wine, Minister of Works Wang Yan and others rose; Yao alone remained seated and said, "Your Majesty received the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people—yet Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own achievement.

sentences.zh: 」上大笑解之。

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed greatly and smoothed the matter over.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed loudly and let the matter pass.

sentences.zh: 座罷，晏呼𤅢共載還令省，欲相撫悅。

translations.literal: When the seating ended, Yan called Yao to ride together back to the Ministry of Works, wishing to soothe and please him.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet ended, Yan invited Yao to ride back with him to the Ministry of Works, hoping to win him over.

sentences.zh: 又正色曰：「君巢窟在何處？

translations.literal: Yao again said with stern countenance: "Where is your nest and den?
translations.idiomatic: Yao said sternly, "Where is your nest and den?

sentences.zh: 」晏初得班劔，𤅢謂之曰：「身家太傅裁得六人。

translations.literal: " Yan had just received ceremonial swords; Yao said to him: "Our family's Grand Tutor received only six men.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had just received ceremonial swords; Yao told him, "Our family's Grand Tutor received only six sword-bearers.

sentences.zh: 君亦何事一朝至此。

translations.literal: What business of yours brings you to this in a single morning?"
translations.idiomatic: What business of yours brings you to this in a single morning?"

sentences.zh: 」晏甚憚之。

translations.literal: " Yan feared him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yan feared him greatly.

sentences.zh: 加領右軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was additionally made General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 兄朏在吳興，論啓公事稽晚，𤅢輙代爲啓，上見非其手迹，被問，見原。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tiao was in Wuxing; discussion memorials on public affairs were late; Yao repeatedly submitted them on his behalf; the emperor saw they were not Tiao's hand and questioned him; he was forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Tiao was in Wuxing and was late submitting official memorials; Yao repeatedly submitted them for him; the emperor noticed the handwriting was not Tiao's and questioned him, but forgave the offense.

sentences.zh: 轉侍中，領太子中庶子，豫州中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant, concurrently Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Director of Selection for Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Palace Attendant, Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Director of Selection for Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，轉散騎常侍，太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattershot Cavalry and Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattershot Cavalry and Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 其年卒。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he died.

sentences.zh: 年四十五。

translations.literal: He was forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 謚簡子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Simple Son.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Simple Son.

sentences.zh: 初，兄朏爲吳興，𤅢於征虜渚送別，朏指𤅢口曰：「此中唯宜飲酒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when his elder brother Tiao was in Wuxing, Yao saw him off at Zhengliu Ford; Tiao pointed at Yao's mouth and said: "In this there is only what suits drinking wine.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when his elder brother Tiao was leaving for Wuxing, Yao saw him off at Zhengliu Ford; Tiao pointed at Yao's mouth and said, "This is fit for nothing but drinking wine.

sentences.zh: 」𤅢建武之初，專以長酣爲事，與劉瑱沈昭略以觴酌交飲，各至數斗。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Jianwu, Yao devoted himself solely to long drinking as his occupation; with Liu Zhen and Shen Zhaolüe he exchanged cups and drank together, each reaching several dou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianwu, Yao devoted himself to long drinking bouts; with Liu Zhen and Shen Zhaolüe he exchanged cups and drank together, each consuming several dou.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗問王儉，當今誰能爲五言詩？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once asked Wang Jian who today can write five-character verse.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once asked Wang Jian who in the present age could write five-character verse.

sentences.zh: 儉對曰：「謝朏得父膏腴；

translations.literal: Jian replied: "Xie Tiao has received his father's rich marrow;
translations.idiomatic: Jian answered, "Xie Tiao has inherited his father's literary richness;

sentences.zh: 江淹有意。

translations.literal: Jiang Yan has intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan has genuine talent."

sentences.zh: 」上起禪靈寺，勑𤅢撰碑文。

translations.literal: " The emperor built Chanling Temple and ordered Yao to compose the stele inscription.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor built Chanling Temple and ordered Yao to compose its stele inscription.

sentences.zh: 王思遠，琅邪臨沂人。

translations.literal: Wang Siyuan was a man of Linyi in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Siyuan came from Linyi in Langya Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尚書令晏從弟也。

translations.literal: He was a younger cousin of Minister of Works Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was a younger cousin of Wang Yan, Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 父羅雲，平西長史。

translations.literal: His father Luoyun was Chief Clerk of the Pacification of the West.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Luoyun was Chief Clerk of the Pacification of the West.

sentences.zh: 思遠八歲，父卒，祖弘之及外祖新安太守羊敬元，竝栖退高尚，故思遠少無仕心。

translations.literal: Siyuan at eight years lost his father; his grandfather Hongzhi and his maternal grandfather Yang Jingyuan, Administrator of Xin'an, both dwelt in retirement and lofty virtue; therefore Siyuan from youth had no mind for office.
translations.idiomatic: When Siyuan was eight his father died; his grandfather Wang Hongzhi and his maternal grandfather Yang Jingyuan, Administrator of Xin'an, both lived in lofty retirement, and so from youth Siyuan had little desire for office.

sentences.zh: 宋建平王景素辟爲南徐州主簿，深見禮遇。

translations.literal: Prince Jianping Jingsu of Song invited him as Master of Records for Southern Xuzhou and treated him with deep courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jianping of Jingsu in the Song recruited him as Master of Records for Southern Xuzhou and treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 景素被誅，左右離散，思遠親視殯葬，手種松柏。

translations.literal: When Jingsu was executed his attendants scattered; Siyuan personally oversaw the encoffining and burial and planted pine and cypress with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingsu was executed his attendants scattered; Siyuan personally oversaw the funeral and planted pine and cypress with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 與廬江何昌宇、沛郡劉璡上表理之，事感朝廷。

translations.literal: Together with He Changyu of Lujiang and Liu Zhen of Pei commandery he submitted a memorial to clear the case; the affair moved the court.
translations.idiomatic: Together with He Changyu of Lujiang and Liu Zhen of Pei Commandery he submitted a memorial to clear the prince's name, and the affair moved the court.

sentences.zh: 景素女廢爲庶人，思遠分衣食以相資贍，年長，爲備笄總，訪求素對，傾家送遣。

translations.literal: Jingsu's daughter was demoted to commoner status; Siyuan shared food and clothing to support her; when she grew older he prepared her hairpin and coming-of-age rites, sought a suitable match, and sent her off at the cost of his whole household.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingsu's daughter was reduced to commoner status, Siyuan shared his food and clothing to support her; when she came of age he prepared her hairpin ceremony, sought a suitable husband, and sent her off at the cost of his entire estate.

sentences.zh: 除晉熙王撫軍行參軍，安成王車騎參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Adjutant on the Pacification Army staff of Prince Jinxi and Adjutant on the Chariots and Cavalry staff of Prince Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Acting Adjutant on Prince Jinxi's Pacification Army staff and Adjutant on Prince Ancheng's Chariots and Cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 建元初，爲長沙王後軍主簿，尚書殿中郎，出補竟陵王征北記室參軍，府遷司徒，仍爲錄事參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he was Rear Army Master of Records for Prince Changsha, Attendant in the Palace Hall of the Masters of Writing, went out to fill the post of Recorder on the Northern Expedition staff of Prince Jingling; when the princely establishment was transferred to Minister of Works he remained Recorder Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianyuan he was Rear Army Master of Records for Prince Changsha and Attendant in the Palace Hall; he was then assigned as Recorder on Prince Jingling's Northern Expedition staff, and when the princely establishment became the Ministry of Works he remained Recorder Adjutant.

sentences.zh: 遷太子中舍人，文惠太子與竟陵王子良素好士，竝蒙賞接。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent; the Literary Heir Apparent and Prince Jingling of Ziliang from of old loved scholars, and both honored and received him.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant of the Heir Apparent; both the Literary Heir Apparent and Prince Jingling of Ziliang had long loved men of learning, and both honored and befriended him.

sentences.zh: 思遠求出爲遠郡，除建安內史。

translations.literal: Siyuan requested to go out to a distant commandery and was appointed Interior Minister of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan asked to be sent to a distant commandery and was appointed Interior Minister of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 長兄思玄卒，思遠友于甚至，表乞自解，不許。

translations.literal: His elder brother Sixuan died; Siyuan's brotherly affection was extreme; he submitted a request to resign of his own accord, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Sixuan died, Siyuan's brotherly grief was profound; he petitioned to resign but was refused.

sentences.zh: 及祥日，又固陳，世祖乃許之。

translations.literal: When the day of the memorial rite arrived, he again firmly stated his case, and Emperor Wu then granted it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the memorial rite he again pressed his case firmly, and Emperor Wu at last granted his request.

sentences.zh: 除中書郎，大司馬諮議。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Secretariat Attendant and Adviser to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and Adviser to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔舉士，竟陵王子良薦思遠及吳郡顧暠之、陳郡殷叡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu ordered the recommendation of scholars; Prince Jingling of Ziliang recommended Siyuan, Gu Haozhi of Wu commandery, and Yin Rui of Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu ordered scholars to be recommended; Prince Jingling of Ziliang recommended Siyuan, Gu Haozhi of Wu Commandery, and Yin Rui of Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王子貞爲吳郡，世祖除思遠爲吳郡丞，以本官行郡事，論者以爲得人。

translations.literal: Prince Shaoling Zizhen was in charge of Wu commandery; Emperor Wu appointed Siyuan as Assistant Administrator of Wu and had him conduct commandery affairs in his existing office; commentators considered this a proper choice of man.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Shaoling of Zizhen held Wu Commandery, Emperor Wu appointed Siyuan as Assistant Administrator and had him run the commandery in his existing capacity; commentators judged this an excellent appointment.

sentences.zh: 以疾解職，還爲司徒諮議參軍，領錄事，轉黃門郎。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he resigned his post, returned as Adviser Adjutant to the Minister of Works, concurrently Recorder, and was transferred to Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness, returned as Adviser Adjutant to the Minister of Works and Recorder, and was then made Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 出爲使持節、都督廣交越三州諸軍事、寧朔將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the three provinces of Guang, Jiao, and Yue, General Who Pacifies the North, Central Commandant Who Pacifies Yue, and Inspector of Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Guang, Jiao, and Yue, General Who Pacifies the North, Central Commandant Who Pacifies Yue, and Inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 高宗輔政，不之任，仍遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao assisted in government he did not go to the appointment and was instead transferred to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao assumed the regency Siyuan did not take up the post and was instead made Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 臨海太守沈昭略贓私，思遠依事劾奏，高宗及思遠從兄晏、昭略叔父文季請止之，思遠不從，案事如故。

translations.literal: Shen Zhaolüe, Administrator of Linhai, was corrupt for private gain; Siyuan impeached him according to the facts; Emperor Gao, Siyuan's cousin Yan, and Zhaolüe's uncle Wenji asked him to stop; Siyuan did not comply and pursued the case as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Zhaolüe, Administrator of Linhai, was found corrupt, Siyuan impeached him on the evidence; Emperor Gao, Siyuan's cousin Wang Yan, and Zhaolüe's uncle Wenji asked him to desist, but he refused and pursued the case.

sentences.zh: 建武中，遷吏部郎。

translations.literal: During Jianwu he was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwu era he was made Director of the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 思遠以從兄晏爲尚書令，不欲竝居內臺權要之職，上表固讓。

translations.literal: Because his cousin Yan was Minister of Works, Siyuan did not wish to hold together with him key posts in the inner administration and submitted a firm memorial of declination.
translations.idiomatic: Because his cousin Wang Yan was Minister of Works, Siyuan did not wish to hold a key inner-court post alongside him and submitted a firm memorial declining the appointment.

sentences.zh: 曰：「近頻煩歸啓，實有微概。

translations.literal: He said: "Recently I have repeatedly troubled you with memorials of return; I truly have a slight grievance.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote, "I have recently troubled Your Majesty with repeated petitions to withdraw, and I do have a private concern.

sentences.zh: 陛下矜遇之厚，古今罕儔。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's generous treatment is thick—rarely matched in past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's gracious treatment of me is rarely matched in history.

sentences.zh: 臣若孤恩，誰當戮力。

translations.literal: If your subject isolates this grace, who will exert strength?
translations.idiomatic: If I turn my back on such grace, who will serve with full devotion?

sentences.zh: 旣自誓輕軀命，不復以塵黷爲疑，正以臣與晏地惟密親，必不宜俱居顯要。

translations.literal: Having sworn to hold my body lightly, I no longer doubt worldly defilement; it is precisely because your subject and Yan are only close kin by station that we must not both hold prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: I have sworn to hold my life lightly and no longer fear worldly stain; it is precisely because Yan and I are close kin that we must not both hold prominent posts at court.

sentences.zh: 慺慺丹赤，守之以死。

translations.literal: Earnest and red-hearted, I guard this unto death.
translations.idiomatic: With earnest loyalty I will guard this principle unto death.

sentences.zh: 臣實庸鄙，無足獎進。

translations.literal: Your subject is truly mediocre and base, unworthy of reward and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: I am truly mediocre and unworthy of promotion.

sentences.zh: 陛下甄拔之旨，要是許其一節。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's intent in selecting and elevating was after all to grant one of my qualities.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's intent in elevating me was to recognize one merit in me.

sentences.zh: 臣果不能以理自固，有乖則哲之明。

translations.literal: If your subject truly cannot hold firm by principle, I would go against the clarity of the discerning sage.
translations.idiomatic: If I cannot hold firm by principle, I would offend Your Majesty's discerning judgment.

sentences.zh: 犯冒之尤，誅責在己，謬賞之私，惟塵聖鑒。

translations.literal: The fault of offense and presumption—punishment and blame rest on myself; the private error of mistaken reward may only cloud the sage mirror.
translations.idiomatic: The fault of presumption is mine alone to bear; any mistaken reward would only cloud Your Majesty's judgment.

sentences.zh: 權其輕重，寧守福心。

translations.literal: Weighing light and heavy, I would rather keep a heart of blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing the matter, I would rather keep peace of mind.

sentences.zh: 且亦緣陛下以德御下，故臣可得以禮進退。

translations.literal: Moreover it is because Your Majesty rules subordinates with virtue that your subject may advance and withdraw according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: It is because Your Majesty rules with virtue that I may advance or withdraw according to propriety.

sentences.zh: 伏願思垂拯宥，不使零墜。

translations.literal: I humbly wish you to think of extending rescue and pardon, and not let me fall to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to extend your mercy and not let me fall to ruin.

sentences.zh: 今若祗膺所忝，三公不足爲泰，犯忤之後，九泉未足爲劇。

translations.literal: If now I reverently accept what shames me, the Three Excellencies are not enough for pride; after offending, the Nine Springs are not enough for severity.
translations.idiomatic: If I now accept this shameful post, even the rank of the Three Excellencies would bring me no joy; after such an offense, even death would not be punishment enough.

sentences.zh: 而臣苟求刑戮，自弃富榮，愚夫不爲，臣亦庶免。

translations.literal: Yet your subject seeks punishment and execution, abandoning wealth and glory—what a fool would not do, your subject also hopes to avoid.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I would rather seek punishment and abandon wealth and glory—what a fool would do, and what I too hope to avoid.

sentences.zh: 此心此志，可怜可矜。

translations.literal: This heart, this will—pitiable and deserving compassion.
translations.idiomatic: This heart and this resolve are pitiable indeed.

sentences.zh: 如其上命必行，請罪非理，聖恩方置之通塗，而臣固求擯壓，自愍自悼，不覺涕流。

translations.literal: If your superior command must be carried out, pleading guilt is unreasonable; sacred grace has just placed me on the open road, yet your subject stubbornly seeks rejection and suppression; pitying and grieving myself, I do not notice tears flowing.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty's command must stand, my plea is unreasonable; Your grace has just cleared my path, yet I stubbornly seek rejection; grieving for myself, I cannot keep back my tears.

sentences.zh: 謹冒鈇鉞，悉心以請。

translations.literal: I respectfully dare the axe and halberd and pour out my heart in request.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully risk your displeasure and pour out my whole heart in this plea.

sentences.zh: 窮則呼天，仰祈一照。

translations.literal: In extremity one calls to Heaven; I look up hoping for one beam of light.
translations.idiomatic: In extremity one cries to Heaven; I look up and beg for a single ray of light.

sentences.zh: 」上知其意，乃改授司徒左長史。

translations.literal: " The emperor understood his intent and thereupon transferred him to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood his intent and transferred him to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，高宗廢立之際，思遠與晏閑言，謂晏曰：「兄荷世祖厚恩，今一旦贊人如此事，彼或可以權計相須，未知兄將來何以自立。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the time of Emperor Gao's deposition and enthronement, Siyuan spoke with Yan in private and said to Yan: "Elder brother, you received thick grace from Emperor Wu; now in a single morning you have assisted others in such an affair—they may need you for schemes of power; I do not know how you will establish yourself in the future.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Gao was deposing and enthroning emperors, Siyuan spoke privately with Yan and said, "Brother, you received great favor from Emperor Wu; now you have aided others in such a coup—they may need you for their schemes; I do not know how you will stand on your own afterward.

sentences.zh: 若及此引決，猶可不失後名。

translations.literal: If you take resolution at this point, you may still not lose your later reputation."
translations.idiomatic: If you act now, you may still preserve your good name."

sentences.zh: 」晏不納。

translations.literal: " Yan did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 及拜驃騎，集會子弟，謂思遠兄思微曰：「隆昌之末，阿戎勸吾自裁，若從其語，豈有今日。

translations.literal: When he was appointed Rapid Cavalry Commander he gathered his sons and nephews and said to Siyuan's elder brother Siwei: "At the end of Longchang, Arong urged me to take my own life; if I had followed his words, how could there be today?
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was appointed Rapid Cavalry Commander he gathered his kin and said to Siyuan's elder brother Siwei, "At the end of Longchang, your brother urged me to take my own life; had I listened, would I be here today?

sentences.zh: 」思遠遽應曰：「如阿戎所見，猶未晚也。

translations.literal: " Siyuan immediately replied: "As Arong saw it, it is still not too late."
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan immediately replied, "As your brother saw it, it is still not too late."

sentences.zh: 」及晏敗，故得無他。

translations.literal: " When Yan was ruined, he therefore suffered no other harm.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan fell, Siyuan therefore escaped further harm.

sentences.zh: 思遠清脩，立身簡潔。

translations.literal: Siyuan was pure in cultivation and simple in establishing himself.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan was pure in conduct and austere in his way of life.

sentences.zh: 衣服牀筵，窮治素凈，賔客來通，輙使人先密覘視，衣服垢穢，方便不前，形儀新楚，乃與促膝。

translations.literal: Clothes and bedding he brought to utmost plain purity; when guests came to visit he always had someone first spy secretly—if clothes were filthy and stained, he would on pretext not advance; if bearing and dress were fresh and neat, only then would he sit knee to knee.
translations.idiomatic: His clothes and bedding were kept scrupulously clean; when guests came he had someone watch them first—if their dress was soiled he would find an excuse not to receive them; only if they were neat and presentable would he sit with them knee to knee.

sentences.zh: 雖然，旣去之後，猶令二人交帚拂其坐處。

translations.literal: Even so, after they had left he still ordered two men to sweep each other's brooms over the place where they had sat.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, after they left he still had two servants sweep the place where they had sat.

sentences.zh: 上從祖弟季敞性甚豪縱，上心非之。

translations.literal: The emperor's younger cousin Jichang by a great-uncle was very arrogant and unrestrained; the emperor's heart disapproved of him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's cousin Jichang was very arrogant and unrestrained, and the emperor disapproved of him.

sentences.zh: 謂季敞曰：「卿可數詣王思遠。」

translations.literal: He said to Jichang: "You may often visit Wang Siyuan."
translations.idiomatic: He told Jichang, "You should visit Wang Siyuan often."

sentences.zh: 上旣誅晏，遷爲侍中，掌優策及起居注。

translations.literal: After the emperor had executed Yan, Siyuan was transferred to Palace Attendant, in charge of superior policy and the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor executed Yan, Siyuan was made Palace Attendant, in charge of court policy and the Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，遷度支尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongyuan he was made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 未拜，卒。

translations.literal: Before he accepted the appointment he died.
