translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume the post he died.

sentences.zh: 年四十九。

translations.literal: He was forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-nine years old.

sentences.zh: 贈太常，謚貞子。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies; his posthumous title was Upright Son.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Ceremonies, with the posthumous title Upright Son.

sentences.zh: 思遠與顧暠之友善。

translations.literal: Siyuan and Gu Haozhi were friendly.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan and Gu Haozhi were close friends.

sentences.zh: 暠之卒後家貧，思遠迎其兒子，經卹甚至。

translations.literal: After Haozhi died his family was poor; Siyuan welcomed his son and saw him through mourning with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: After Haozhi died, leaving his family in poverty, Siyuan took in his son and cared for him through mourning with the greatest devotion.

sentences.zh: 暠之字士明。

translations.literal: Haozhi, courtesy name Shiming.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Haozhi, whose courtesy name was Shiming,

sentences.zh: 少孤，好學有義行。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he loved learning and had conduct of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: was orphaned young, loved learning, and was known for righteous conduct.

sentences.zh: 初舉秀才，歷宦府閤。

translations.literal: He was first recommended as Cultivated Talent and passed through offices in the princely establishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was first recommended as Cultivated Talent and served in various princely establishments.

sentences.zh: 永明末，爲太子中舍人，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongming he was Attendant of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongming era he was Attendant of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 隆昌初，爲安西諮議，兼著作，與思遠竝屬文章。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longchang he was Adviser to the Pacification of the West and concurrently Compiler, and with Siyuan both belonged to the literary circle.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Longchang he was Adviser to the Pacification of the West and Compiler, and he and Siyuan were both noted writers.

sentences.zh: 建武初，以疾歸家，高宗手詔與思遠曰：「此人殊可惜。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, on grounds of illness he returned home; Emperor Gao wrote a personal edict to Siyuan saying: "This man is especially worth cherishing.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianwu he returned home on grounds of illness; Emperor Gao wrote personally to Siyuan, "This man is especially worth cherishing.

sentences.zh: 」就拜中散大夫。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon appointed Grand Master of Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon appointed Grand Master of Leisure.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: He died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 思微，永元中爲江州長史，爲陳伯之所殺。

translations.literal: Siwei, during Yongyuan was Chief Clerk of Jiang province and was killed by Chen Bozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Siwei served as Chief Clerk of Jiang Province during Yongyuan and was killed by Chen Bozhi.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：德成爲上，藝成爲下。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Virtue completed is upper; art completed is lower.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: Virtue ranks above, accomplishment in arts below.

sentences.zh: 觀夫二三子之治身，豈直清體雅業，取隆基構；

translations.literal: Observing how these two or three men ordered their persons—is it only pure bodies and elegant occupations, taking lofty foundations for structure?
translations.idiomatic: Considering how these men ordered their lives—was it only purity of body and elegance of craft, or the building of a great foundation?

sentences.zh: 行禮蹈義，可以勉物風規云。

translations.literal: Practicing ritual and treading righteousness—they can encourage the customs and norms of things.
translations.idiomatic: By practicing ritual and upholding righteousness they could encourage the manners of the age.

sentences.zh: 君子之居世，所謂美矣！

translations.literal: The gentleman's dwelling in the world—this is what is called beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Such is the beauty of how a gentleman lives in the world!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：江纂世業，有聞時陂。

translations.literal: In praise it is said: Jiang continued the family enterprise, renowned on the slope of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Jiang continued the family tradition and won renown in his time.

sentences.zh: 何申舊主，辭出乎義。

translations.literal: He spoke for his old lord; his words arose from righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke for his former lord, his words born of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 謝獻壽觴，載色載刺。

translations.literal: Xie offered the cup of longevity, bearing color and bearing sting.
translations.idiomatic: Xie raised the cup of longevity, with wit and with bite.

sentences.zh: 思遠退食，沖心篤寄。

translations.literal: Siyuan withdrew to eat, with pure heart and deep trust.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan withdrew from office, his heart pure and his devotion deep.
